newsitem.title: USA: UNR hires search firm to find CEO.
newsitem.headline: UNR hires search firm to find CEO.

text.p: UNR Industries Inc said Thursday it retained an executive search firm to help its board in recruiting a new president and chief executive officer.
It said the new executive would replace Thomas Gildehaus, who will retire from UNR once a new president and chief executive officer is named.

Separately, UNR said it sold its Real Time Solutions Inc subsidiary to Pinnacle Automation. The sale concludes a divestiture program announced January 26, 1996, when the company disclosed its intent to sell four of five remaining operating units in order to focus on its UNR ROHN division.
The four units were sold for a total of about $162 million, the company said.
Extraordinary dividends distributed to shareholders of $2 per share were paid September 27, and $0.35 per share will be paid December 23 along with a regular dividend of $0.25 per share.
UNR's sole remaining operating unit, Peoria, Ill.-based UNR ROHN, supplies towers and shelters to the telecommunications industry.
Effective January 31, 1997, UNR said it will close its Chicago office and move the corporate office and its responsibilities to ROHN operating headquarters in Peoria.

Chairman Gene Locks said, "ROHN has significant opportunities to continue the double-digit growth rate it has experienced over the last three years." He said UNR's board approved a $25 million capital expansion program to enable ROHN to pursue growth.
